For posterior contrast Z with E[Z]=0, the unconditional AA and AB pair densities with respect to M×M are 1+ZZ' and 1−ZZ'. Conditional independence and revealed random channel tags give exactly Delta=1/2 E[h(−ZZ')−h(ZZ')]. The absolutely uniformly convergent expansion h(t)=t+sum_{n>=2}(-1)^n t^n/[n(n−1)] on [-1,1] yields the sum of squares sum_{j>=1}(E Z^(2j+1))^2/[(2j)(2j+1)]. Zero gap iff all odd moments vanish, equivalent by compact moment uniqueness to sign symmetry. Binary equality and weak-signal remainder follow from centering and the same series. value.rationale: A precise structural solution to a natural statistical experiment comparison: every pair of conjugate binary-input channels can be classified by the odd moments of its posterior score. The finite-alphabet identity establishes the entire sign and equality structure, including nontrivial equality for unequal two-symbol experiments. This settles an all-parameter boundary left at numerical indications in the earlier channel literature and quantifies the first weak-signal asymmetry contribution. It goes beyond known isolated JS counterexamples or the textbook mutual-information chain rule.
